name: Col-hozeh
overview: Col-hozeh was a male official from the tribe of Judah, serving in the district of Mizpah. He is noted in Scripture as an important administrative figure during the post-exilic period. His association with the tribe of Judah is confirmed in Nehemiah 11:4-5.
namesAndTitles: The name Col-hozeh means 'every seer,' indicating a title or designation related to vision or insight. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 3:15 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Col-hozeh is identified as the father of Shallum, as mentioned in Nehemiah 3:15. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Baruch and explicitly the father of Hazaiah according to Nehemiah 11:5. These relationships establish his role as a patriarch within his family.
scriptureSignificance: Col-hozeh's significance lies in his role as an official overseeing the district of Mizpah during the restoration of Jerusalem's walls, reflecting the organized leadership among the returning exiles. His tribal affiliation with Judah situates him within the community responsible for rebuilding and reestablishing the city. Through his family connections, he contributed to the continuity of leadership during this crucial period.
